chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the food of the People of the Book and what is permissible from it. He said: The grains.

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ: People of the Book (Christians, Jews, Sabians)

ai.seo_question: What food of the People of the Book is permissible for Shia Muslims to eat according to hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that 'al-hubub' (grains and cereals) are inherently pure and permissible, distinguishing them from other foods that may require specific conditions. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of 'istishab al-taharah' (presumption of purity) for basic plant-based foods, facilitating social and economic interaction with the People of the Book. It underscores the practical flexibility in Shia dietary laws while maintaining theological boundaries regarding idolatrous sacrifices.
